details: For checking tasks, work activities, work context, technology skills, interest code (AC), and preparation level (Job Zone Four).

Main tasks include organizing and assembling raw materials into complete productions; selecting and combining the most effective shots; trimming and reassembling to specified lengths; switching camera angles; inserting and sequencing music, dialogue, and sound effects; using editing, titling, and effects equipment; checking key numbers and timecodes; collaborating with audio, music, and effects departments; screening, reviewing, and revising; marking starting and ending frames; attending screenings; and discussing editing direction with producers and directors.

Work context: 97% have regular schedules; 62% work 40 hours weekly and 38% more than 40 hours; 62% sit continually or almost continually and 34% more than half the time; precision and accuracy are extremely important to 51% and very important to 42%; 71% face strict deadlines daily; 58% have constant contact with others; 90% consider work pace not determined by equipment speed.

O*NET's national wage page (onetonline.org/link/localwages/27-4032.00) gives this occupation's national percentiles: annual wages of USD 40,280 at 10%, USD 52,720 at 25%, USD 75,420 at the median, USD 105,310 at 75%, and USD 148,550 at 90%; corresponding hourly wages are USD 19.37, 25.35, 36.26, 50.63, and 71.42.
